source.title: PAC-Bayes Compression Bounds So Tight That They Can Explain Generalization
source.authors: Sanae Lotfi; Marc Finzi; Sanyam Kapoor; Andres Potapczynski; Micah Goldblum; A. Wilson

record.tranche_reason: Uses PAC-Bayes compression bounds to examine architecture, dataset structure, equivariance, optimizer stochasticity, model size and double descent as explanations of generalization.
record.gate_note: The study reports bounds and compressibility, not direct held-out test errors for the architecture comparisons. Double-descent test error is shown in a figure without recoverable numerical values. Cited optimizer and generalization results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: Appendix I reports the study's own held-out test-error results from widening ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with 20% label noise. The descending branch at larger widths bears on V2 in a new setting, even though exact values are unreadable. The other comparisons primarily measure compression bounds rather than the outcomes named in the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the authors argue that compression provides strong generalization guarantees and explains several effects of dataset and architectural structure. Similar bounds under full-batch and stochastic training suggest stochasticity is unnecessary for these guarantees. Their bounds favor smaller models and leave the generalization advantage of larger models unexplained.
record.recipe_differences: Trains and quantizes models in structured random subspaces, then uses PAC-Bayes compression bounds rather than the original studies' direct test-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset structure and model architecture affect compressibility and bounds; equivariance benefits the bound on rotationally symmetric data but not ordinary MNIST. The model-size ablation finds weaker bounds for larger models. Bounds are similar for SGD and full-batch training.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter-matched CNNs have tighter compression bounds than MLPs on ordinary CIFAR-10; shuffling pixels removes that bound advantage, and shuffled-label bounds are vacuous.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dataset and architectural structure affect compressibility and PAC-Bayes bounds. Bound ordering does not establish held-out error ordering.

fits_no_version.finding: Rotationally equivariant WideResNets have better compression bounds on RotMNIST, but the advantage disappears on ordinary MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching architectural symmetry to dataset symmetry can improve compressibility and generalization guarantees.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-batch and stochastic training obtain similar best bounds in several settings, using different training budgets and recipes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-vacuous compression guarantees can be obtained without stochastic optimization under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: The model-size ablation favors relatively small models under the PAC-Bayes bound, while compressed dataset description length favors larger models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These compression bounds do not explain the generalization advantage of larger models; alternative compression criteria can prefer different sizes.

record.problems: The architecture and equivariance findings are expressed as PAC-Bayes bounds rather than direct test-error measurements. The double-descent figure has no recoverable numerical values in the supplied text. The authors note that their bounds favor smaller models and do not explain why larger models often generalize better.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: the relevant architecture and equivariance outcomes are reported as bounds, not the direct test-error measures specified by the versions; double-descent test-error outcomes are figure-only without numerical values.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and random-label training accuracy and held-out accuracy are not reported. Vacuous random-label bounds do not establish chance held-out accuracy.

The original one-hidden-layer networks, training to convergence without explicit regularization, and the location of the zero-training-error threshold are not established for the reported width sweep. Continued improvement outside the plotted width range is untested.
CNN–MLP comparisons report bounds, not comparative held-out errors. Local-connectivity interventions, learned sparse connections, and initialization from trained convolutional networks are untested.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison of held-out performance.
No comparison of held-out performance across batch sizes under equal epoch budgets. Full-batch training uses 3000 epochs versus 500 for stochastic training, with different optimization settings.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking against alternative generalization measures.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Unreadable numerical values do not invalidate an explicitly stated qualitative test-error result. Figure 7's test-error descending branch bears on V2; its interpolation-region peak is a separate double-descent finding. No missing entry is added because rows_left_out already declares the omitted figure-only test-error results.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out accuracy for natural-label and random-label training under the same recipe.
Reports a ResNet-18 width sweep with label noise and a double-descent result, not the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU experiments; numerical test errors are not provided in the text.

Compares CNN and MLP generalization bounds on CIFAR-10 and reports equivariance-bound comparisons, but does not report the direct test-error comparisons or local-connectivity interventions named in the version.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers against SGD on held-out performance.
Does not vary batch size or compare large and small batch performance.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and measure the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: The descending branch at larger widths in the noisy-label CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 sweep.
relationships.reason: Appendix I and Figure 7 explicitly report double descent in last-epoch test error, including improvement at larger widths. This supports the width-improvement component; interpolation and convergence are not established. Based on text; no row ids exist.
relationships.display_finding: The reported second descent remains unverified, with interpolation and convergence also unestablished.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
